newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, still stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, still stuck in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Tuesday in a moderate session, but relatively steady physical prices kept the market in its recent technical range, industry sources said.
May slipped 1.6 cents to close at $1.937 per million British thermal units. June settled 2.1 cents lower at $1.975. Other deferreds ended on either side of unchanged.

"The Merc is still looking for direction, but I wouldn't want to be too long from August to October. It wasn't'a good sign when May couldn't get above $2 (last week) even with colder weather," said one East Coast trader.
While cooler Midwest and Northeast temperatures later this week should keep cash relatively steady near-term, few saw much upside until broader cooling loads kick in.
Chart traders agreed recent ranges were intact, with May trendline support in the $1.89 area and more buying likely at $1.85 and $1.825. Resistance was seen at $1.975, $1.99, $2.05 and $2.095.
Estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report ranged from a draw of 40 bcf to a build of 13.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices stayed little changed Tuesday in the high-$1.90s. Midcontinent pipes also were relatively flat in the mid-$1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was talked several cents softer in the $2.35 area.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 0.6 cent to $2.137. NYMEX said 29,943 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 23,940.
No NYMEX Permian or Alberta gas contracts traded Tuesday.

On the KCBT, May finished one cent lower at $1.81, while deferreds ended steady to up 1.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 12.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 178 lots changed hands, up from Monday's total of 153.
